Subject: Request for GDPR artefacts and subprocessor attestations

Hi Tessa,

Hope you're well. We're starting procurement for a pilot integration and need to validate a few privacy items before moving to SOW/signature. Can you provide the following so we can progress?

- A redacted excerpt of your Article 30 processing register (records of processing activities) relevant to our use case.
- Art. 28 processor agreement/annex (or the specific DPA template) and a copy of the current subprocessor list + latest attestations.
- DPIA support: any completed DPIA templates or a short note on how Redwood approaches DPIA evidence for customer-specific processing.
- Evidence of transfer safeguards (SCCs or onshore routing options) and whether any subprocessors process data outside the EU/US.
- SOC 2 Type II certificate (most recent) or equivalent audit report.

I've attached our standard GDPR questionnaire (gdpr-questionnaire.xlsx) to make this concrete. Timeline: can you confirm if 10 business days is feasible? Procurement will coordinate signatures once we have the DPA and attestations.

Thanks — appreciate a single ZIP or Drive link if easier.

Laura Jenkins
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Acme Health

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. We'll pull together a concise evidence packet. Initial notes:

- We'll provide a redacted Art.30 excerpt scoped to your pilot (data categories, purposes, retention).
- Attaching our standard DPA template (Art.28) and the canonical subprocessor roster; we'll include a signed attestation pdf for subprocessors where available.
- For DPIA support, I'll coordinate a short walkthrough with Marissa (privacy operations) and Aditya (technical ops) so we can map the controls to your questionnaire responses.
- Transfer safeguards: Redwood offers SCCs + onshore routing options in select regions; we'll flag any subprocessors with non-US/EU processing.
- SOC 2 Type II: we can provide the latest report under NDA; suggest we share via secure Drive link.

10 business days is tight but doable if procurement confirms the scope is limited to the pilot. Can you confirm whether the pilot will process patient identifiers, or only pseudonymized tokens? That affects the DPIA depth.

I'll compile a zip and share a link; Marissa, can you lead the evidence assembly? Aditya, please pull the Art.30 extract and subprocessor attestations.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Privacy
Redwood Inference
